tools.result:
# Brindle 3.2 documentation

Brindle is an embeddable message-queue library for Go and Rust services.

## Ordering

Messages are delivered in the order they were published within one queue. The guarantee holds per queue, across all
consumers of that queue, as long as the queue has a single writer.

## Flow control

Each consumer may hold at most 10,000 unacknowledged messages. When a consumer falls further behind, Brindle drops
the oldest unacknowledged message to make room for the new one. The drop is not reported to the publisher or the
consumer; the only trace is the counter `brindle_dropped_total`. Raise `max_unacked` (up to 50,000) or add consumers
if a drop is not acceptable.

## Persistence

Queues are kept in memory and written to a write-ahead log every 200 ms by default (`wal_interval`).
1:# Forum thread: "Brindle or Quarrel?"

final.result:
When a Brindle consumer falls behind, Brindle quietly throws away messages it hasn't delivered yet (`sources/brindle-docs-3.2.md`, "Flow control"):

- **Limit:** each consumer can hold up to 10,000 unacknowledged messages.
- **What happens past the limit:** each new message pushes out the oldest unacknowledged one, which is dropped.
- **No warning:** neither the publisher nor the consumer is told. The only sign is the counter `brindle_dropped_total`.
- **What you can do:** raise `max_unacked` (the most it allows is 50,000) or add more consumers.

That counter is worth putting an alert on, since nothing else reports the loss. The forum thread names Brindle only in its title and adds nothing on this. A note from an earlier session already says the same as the docs, so I didn't store a new one.
